rv.q: As a result, empathy is squelched and the work of one of history's most compassionate novels is reduced to an alienating experience that does the opposite of draw you into the tale.
Director Mikael Burke’s expert handling of Brendan Pelsue’s intricately-detailed script is an artistic achievement.
The Midwest premiere of Brendan Pelsue’s A Tale of Two Cities now on view at Theatre Wit is a dynamic, entertaining, thought provoking experience of theatre.
Burke's character-driven direction and the stellar ensemble warrant even-handedness.
Although the storytelling intrigues and the acting is good in this production, the show is long… 2 hours and forty-five minutes.
The overall effect of this version of a “Tale of Two Cities” was quite satisfying and thought provoking.
If you like history, and care about the revolution and what politics can thrust on a nation, this is one to watch.
